children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Now, could you tell me who Alex lives with? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does live with me, but his other parent also lives with us in the same house.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's perfectly fine – Child Benefit can be claimed when the child lives with you, even if both parents are in the same household. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so you'd need to decide between yourselves who will make the claim.

Next, could you tell me if anyone is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually his other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim for Alex yourself. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

If you'd like to become the claimant instead, you would need to discuss this with Alex's other parent. They would need to stop their claim, and then you could start a new one. Alternatively, if there's a dispute about who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) can make a decision based on the circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know, or would you like me to provide a summary of your eligibility based on the information you've shared?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see, that makes sense. Yes, could you please give me a summary of my eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

However, since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you are not able to make a separate claim. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

---

**Overall Summary:** You are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because his other parent already has an active claim for him. If you'd like to become the claimant, you would need to arrange for the current claim to be stopped first, and then you could apply.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, please don't hesitate to ask. I'm happy to help!
